cases.prompt: I have a model.pt file. How do I serve it on Triton?
expected_behavior: Explain the TorchScript platform form, model repository layout, and write a minimal config.pbtxt
cases.ground_truth: Explain the TorchScript platform form, model repository layout, and write a minimal config.pbtxt.

cases.prompt: Serve this scripted ResNet50 .pt on Triton with dynamic batching.
expected_behavior: Build a config.pbtxt with platform: pytorch_libtorch, max_batch_size, dynamic_batching block, instance_group KIND_GPU
cases.ground_truth: Build a config.pbtxt with platform: pytorch_libtorch, max_batch_size, dynamic_batching block, instance_group KIND_GPU.

cases.prompt: I built a .pt2 using torch.export + aoti_compile_and_package. Serve it.
expected_behavior: Explain backend: pytorch + platform: torch_aoti, device-baked warning, instance_group matching export device
cases.ground_truth: Explain backend: pytorch + platform: torch_aoti, device-baked warning, instance_group matching export device.

cases.prompt: I have model.pt2 exported on CPU. Deploy it.
expected_behavior: Config with torch_aoti + KIND_CPU
Warn that archive is CPU-only
cases.ground_truth: Config with torch_aoti + KIND_CPU.

cases.prompt: Export a PyTorch model to PT2 for GPU serving on Triton.
expected_behavior: Give the torch.export + Dim recipe with .cuda() on model and sample, package, and deploy with KIND_GPU
cases.ground_truth: Give the torch.export + Dim recipe with .cuda() on model and sample, package, and deploy with KIND_GPU.

cases.prompt: Write a config.pbtxt for a PyTorch model that takes two FP32 tensors.
expected_behavior: Produce a complete config with INPUT__0, INPUT__1, OUTPUT__0 or forward-arg names
cases.ground_truth: Produce a complete config with INPUT__0, INPUT__1, OUTPUT__0 or forward-arg names.

cases.prompt: Should I use TorchScript or PT2 for my new model?
expected_behavior: Explain: PT2 is the forward path if torch.export works for the model; TorchScript is legacy but widely compatible
cases.ground_truth: Explain: PT2 is the forward path if torch.export works for the model; TorchScript is legacy but widely compatible.

cases.prompt: backend: pytorch or platform: pytorch_libtorch?
expected_behavior: Explain the three forms and when each applies
cases.ground_truth: Explain the three forms and when each applies.

cases.prompt: Deploy a PyTorch model using the Python runtime path with model.py.
expected_behavior: Explain backend: pytorch + runtime: model.py form, cite L0_pytorch_python_runtime example
cases.ground_truth: Explain backend: pytorch + runtime: model.py form, cite L0_pytorch_python_runtime example.

cases.prompt: Can I name my TorchScript file something other than model.pt?
expected_behavior: Yes, set default_model_filename in config.pbtxt
cases.ground_truth: Yes, set default_model_filename in config.pbtxt.

cases.prompt: I want my PT2 archive called resnet50.pt2 not model.pt2.
expected_behavior: default_model_filename: "resnet50.pt2"
cases.ground_truth: default_model_filename: "resnet50.pt2".

cases.prompt: config.pbtxt has TYPE_BF16 and Triton says unsupported datatype. Fix.
expected_behavior: Explain BF16 is not supported by PyTorch backend
Options: cast to FP16/FP32, use ONNX backend, or TensorRT
cases.ground_truth: Explain BF16 is not supported by PyTorch backend.

cases.prompt: My PT2 model needs BF16. Server rejects it with Unsupported datatype TYPE_BF16.
expected_behavior: Same recommendation: cast or switch backend
cases.ground_truth: Same recommendation: cast or switch backend.

cases.prompt: Can I serve an FP8 PyTorch model on Triton?
expected_behavior: No
FP8 is not supported in the PyTorch backend
Suggest TensorRT
cases.ground_truth: No.

cases.prompt: My model has UINT32 inputs. Triton logs unsupported datatype TYPE_UINT32.
expected_behavior: Cast to INT64 or switch to ONNX backend
Cite L0_libtorch_io_types
cases.ground_truth: Cast to INT64 or switch to ONNX backend.

cases.prompt: The docs say FP16 is blank for PyTorch. Can I use it?
expected_behavior: FP16 is supported by both `pytorch_libtorch` and `torch_aoti` despite the docs table being stale
Cite libtorch_utils.cc
cases.ground_truth: FP16 is supported by both `pytorch_libtorch` and `torch_aoti` despite the docs table being stale.

cases.prompt: Triton logs: unable to find '/models/foo/1/model.pt' for model instance 'foo'.
expected_behavior: Place model.pt at 1/model.pt or set default_model_filename
cases.ground_truth: Place model.pt at 1/model.pt or set default_model_filename.

cases.prompt: Triton: PyTorch inductor model file "..." is unreachable or inaccessible.
expected_behavior: PT2 file missing
Place model.pt2 at 1/model.pt2 or set default_model_filename
cases.ground_truth: PT2 file missing.

cases.prompt: PT2 won't load: configuration expects 1 inputs, but model expects 2 inputs.
expected_behavior: Match input count in config.pbtxt to the exported call spec
Account for control, state, batch inputs separately
cases.ground_truth: Match input count in config.pbtxt to the exported call spec.

cases.prompt: Triton says Incorrect device passed to aoti_runner_cpu.
expected_behavior: PT2 archive was exported on wrong device
Re-export on target device
cases.ground_truth: PT2 archive was exported on wrong device.

cases.prompt: Triton: failed to load model 'foo': TorchScript archive error.
expected_behavior: Rebuild in matching PyTorch version container
Check for opset drift
cases.ground_truth: Rebuild in matching PyTorch version container.

cases.prompt: Triton: 'OUTPUT__0' is a scalar which is not supported.
expected_behavior: Wrap return with torch.tensor(...)
cases.ground_truth: Wrap return with torch.tensor(...).

cases.prompt: Multiple inputs of kind DictType were detected.
expected_behavior: Only one Dict[str, Tensor] input allowed
Collapse or use Tensor-only inputs
cases.ground_truth: Only one Dict[str, Tensor] input allowed.

cases.prompt: An input of type 'List[int]' was detected in the model.
expected_behavior: Only Tensor and Dict[str, Tensor] inputs are supported
Refactor forward()
cases.ground_truth: Only Tensor and Dict[str, Tensor] inputs are supported.

cases.prompt: PyTorch model 'rnn' is using sequence batching with state but not all inputs and outputs follow the <name>__<index> naming convention.
expected_behavior: Rename every input and output to <name>__<index>
Required for stateful sequence batching
cases.ground_truth: Rename every input and output to <name>__<index>.

cases.prompt: PT2: Sequence control input must be addressed using ordinal INPUT__<index>.
expected_behavior: Switch sequence control and state names to INPUT__<i> / OUTPUT__<i>
cases.ground_truth: Switch sequence control and state names to INPUT__<i> / OUTPUT__<i>.

cases.prompt: Triton: Failed to dlopen MODEL_INIT_LIBRARY "/models/foo/1/libinit.so".
expected_behavior: Check file exists, architecture matches, ldd for missing deps
cases.ground_truth: Check file exists, architecture matches, ldd for missing deps.

cases.prompt: MODEL_INIT_LIBRARY does not export 'triton_pytorch_model_init'.
expected_behavior: Library must export extern "C" void triton_pytorch_model_init(const char*, int)
Add the symbol and rebuild
cases.ground_truth: Library must export extern "C" void triton_pytorch_model_init(const char*, int).

cases.prompt: model configuration must contain at least one input, none were specified.
expected_behavior: Add input [ { ... } ] block to config.pbtxt
cases.ground_truth: Add input [ { ... } ] block to config.pbtxt.

cases.prompt: model configuration must contain at least one output.
expected_behavior: Add output [ { ... } ] block to config.pbtxt
cases.ground_truth: Add output [ { ... } ] block to config.pbtxt.

cases.prompt: Can I name my config inputs to match the forward() argument names?
expected_behavior: Yes, FORWARD_ARGUMENT is the first resolver tried
Explain the 3 rules
cases.ground_truth: Yes, FORWARD_ARGUMENT is the first resolver tried.

cases.prompt: What's the INPUT__0 convention?
expected_behavior: NAMED_INDEX: <name>__<integer>, double underscore delimiter
cases.ground_truth: NAMED_INDEX: <name>__<integer>, double underscore delimiter.

cases.prompt: What do I name inputs in a PT2 config.pbtxt?
expected_behavior: Either call-spec names (ARGS[0], KWARGS[k]) or ordinals (INPUT__0)
Both work
cases.ground_truth: Either call-spec names (ARGS[0], KWARGS[k]) or ordinals (INPUT__0).

cases.prompt: My PT2 model returns one Tensor. What's the output name?
expected_behavior: RESULT or OUTPUT__0
Both resolve to the single tensor
cases.ground_truth: RESULT or OUTPUT__0.

cases.prompt: My TorchScript model loaded READY but gives wrong results. Config inputs are named 'a_input' and 'b_input' but the model is forward(a, b).
expected_behavior: Neither 'a_input' nor 'b_input' matches a forward() arg, so FORWARD_ARGUMENT fails; neither follows '<name>__<index>', so NAMED_INDEX also fails; STRICT_CONFIG_ORDERING fires and silently maps by position
Rename to INPUT__0 / INPUT__1 or use names that exactly match the forward() args
cases.ground_truth: Neither 'a_input' nor 'b_input' matches a forward() arg, so FORWARD_ARGUMENT fails; neither follows '<name>__<index>', so NAMED_INDEX also fails; STRICT_CONFIG_ORDERING fires and silently maps by position.

cases.prompt: How do I enable CUDA cache cleaning on TorchScript?
expected_behavior: parameters { key: "ENABLE_CACHE_CLEANING" value { string_value: "true" } }
cases.ground_truth: parameters { key: "ENABLE_CACHE_CLEANING" value { string_value: "true" } }.

cases.prompt: Cache cleaning on a PT2 model.
expected_behavior: parameters { key: "CACHE_CLEANING_ENABLED" value { string_value: "true" } }
Note the different name versus TorchScript
cases.ground_truth: parameters { key: "CACHE_CLEANING_ENABLED" value { string_value: "true" } }.

cases.prompt: How do I limit PyTorch to 4 threads per model?
expected_behavior: Set INTRA_OP_THREAD_COUNT but warn it is process-global; first model to load wins
cases.ground_truth: Set INTRA_OP_THREAD_COUNT but warn it is process-global; first model to load wins.

cases.prompt: What does INFERENCE_MODE do?
expected_behavior: Guards execution with c10::InferenceMode, strictly stronger than NoGrad
Default true
cases.ground_truth: Guards execution with c10::InferenceMode, strictly stronger than NoGrad.

cases.prompt: Enable weight sharing across instances.
expected_behavior: ENABLE_WEIGHT_SHARING true
Warn: not compatible with sequence batching
cases.ground_truth: ENABLE_WEIGHT_SHARING true.

cases.prompt: Disable cuDNN for reproducibility.
expected_behavior: DISABLE_CUDNN true
cases.ground_truth: DISABLE_CUDNN true.

cases.prompt: ENABLE_JIT_PROFILING false, will Triton force true?
expected_behavior: No
The flag is tri-state: unset means libtorch default, false means explicitly off
cases.ground_truth: No.

cases.prompt: Load external embedding weights before my PT2 loads.
expected_behavior: Use MODEL_INIT_LIBRARY
Provide stub .so example with triton_pytorch_model_init
cases.ground_truth: Use MODEL_INIT_LIBRARY.

cases.prompt: My PT2 fails when batch > 1. What's wrong?
expected_behavior: Archive was exported without torch.export.Dim on batch
Re-export with dynamic batch dim >= max_batch_size
cases.ground_truth: Archive was exported without torch.export.Dim on batch.

cases.prompt: torch.export says: You marked batch as dynamic but your code specialized it to constant 1.
expected_behavior: Sample input had batch=1
Use batch > 1 sample (e.g. torch.randn(2, ...)) so export does not specialize
cases.ground_truth: Sample input had batch=1.

cases.prompt: Does PT2 work on RHEL?
expected_behavior: No
AOT Inductor not available on RHEL manylinux builds as of 26.10
cases.ground_truth: No.

cases.prompt: Can I use TYPE_STRING on a PT2 model?
expected_behavior: No
AOT Inductor is tensor-only
Use TorchScript for 1-D List[str], or ONNX
cases.ground_truth: No.

cases.prompt: Can I use TYPE_STRING for CONTROL_SEQUENCE_CORRID in sequence batching on PT2?
expected_behavior: Explain TYPE_STRING is not supported for CORRID on the PT2 platform
Recommend TYPE_INT32 or TYPE_INT64 instead
cases.ground_truth: TYPE_STRING CORRID is not supported on PT2. Use TYPE_INT32 or TYPE_INT64.

cases.prompt: Set up sequence batching with state on TorchScript.
expected_behavior: Use NAMED_INDEX naming (INPUT__0, OUTPUT__0) for every input and output
Add a sequence_batching block to config.pbtxt
Add a control_input block covering START, END, READY, and CORRID
cases.ground_truth: NAMED_INDEX naming, sequence_batching block, control_input block.

cases.prompt: How do I do implicit-state sequence batching on PT2?
expected_behavior: Explain from code-comment spec: forward accepts control+state as regular args, returns new state
Ordinal naming required
Use INT64 CORRID
cases.ground_truth: Explain from code-comment spec: forward accepts control+state as regular args, returns new state.

cases.prompt: Multi-GPU PyTorch model. How do I place it?
expected_behavior: KIND_MODEL so the model's own .to(device) wins
Warn about three behavioral differences from KIND_GPU
cases.ground_truth: KIND_MODEL so the model's own .to(device) wins.

cases.prompt: My PyTorch model on Triton has high latency under concurrent requests. How do I scale throughput?
expected_behavior: Explain the PyTorch backend is BLOCKING (one request per instance at a time)
Add more entries to instance_group to run requests in parallel
Do not try to add threads per instance
cases.ground_truth: Backend is blocking. Scale by adding instance_group entries, not threads.

cases.prompt: First TorchScript request is slow.
expected_behavior: JIT compiles on first invocation
Add model_warmup with representative shapes
cases.ground_truth: JIT compiles on first invocation.

cases.prompt: I set INTRA_OP_THREAD_COUNT = 4 on one model and 8 on another. Why doesn't the second one apply?
expected_behavior: Explain INTRA_OP_THREAD_COUNT is process-global, not per-model
The first model to load locks in the value; later models with different values are ignored
Workaround: load the model with the largest INTRA_OP value first, or run separate tritonserver processes
cases.ground_truth: INTRA_OP_THREAD_COUNT is process-global; the first model to load wins.

cases.prompt: Where are PyTorch inference metrics?
expected_behavior: Standard Triton /metrics on port 8002
Nothing PyTorch-specific
cases.ground_truth: Standard Triton /metrics on port 8002.

cases.prompt: I pip install torch in tritonserver container and it doesn't match libtorch.
expected_behavior: tritonserver container ships libtorch but not Python torch
Build artifacts in nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.10-py3 for ABI match
cases.ground_truth: tritonserver container ships libtorch but not Python torch.

cases.prompt: Show me a curl inference request for a PyTorch model.
expected_behavior: Provide KFServing v2 JSON POST to /v2/models/<name>/infer
cases.ground_truth: Provide KFServing v2 JSON POST to /v2/models/<name>/infer.

cases.prompt: Send a large tensor via binary extension.
expected_behavior: Set Inference-Header-Content-Length and send tensor bytes after the JSON header
cases.ground_truth: Set Inference-Header-Content-Length and send tensor bytes after the JSON header.

cases.prompt: I have a custom TorchScript op in libmycustom.so.
expected_behavior: LD_PRELOAD the library when launching tritonserver with LD_LIBRARY_PATH including /opt/tritonserver/backends/pytorch
cases.ground_truth: LD_PRELOAD the library when launching tritonserver with LD_LIBRARY_PATH including /opt/tritonserver/backends/pytorch.

cases.prompt: Why do my int8 traced-model values overflow when converted to int32 on GPU?
expected_behavior: Explain this is a known upstream PyTorch bug for traced int8 to int32 conversion on GPU
Suggest scripting the model instead of tracing
Or cast inputs to int32 or int64 before sending them to the server
cases.ground_truth: Upstream PyTorch bug. Script instead of trace, or cast inputs to int32 or int64.

cases.prompt: I have a model.onnx. How do I serve on Triton?
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
Point to triton-onnx-model-repository
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: I have a model.plan from trtexec. How do I serve?
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
Point to triton-tensorrt-model-repository
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: Train a PyTorch model on 8 GPUs.
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
This is training, not inference serving
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: Deploy my model with TorchServe.
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
Different product
Point to TorchServe docs
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: Serve Llama-3 with vLLM via Dynamo.
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
Dynamo deployment path, different skill
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: Load a TensorFlow SavedModel.
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
TensorFlow backend, different skill
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: How do I use torch.nn.Linear?
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
General PyTorch API question, not Triton deployment
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: My app loads a model.pt file directly with torch.load. It's slow.
expected_behavior: Decline using this skill
Explain the user is loading the model inside their own app, not deploying on Triton
Suggest PyTorch optimization docs (torch.compile, quantization) or recommend deploying on Triton for better performance
cases.ground_truth: Out of scope for this skill. User runs the model inside their app, not on Triton.

cases.prompt: Package my .pt for PyTorch Mobile.
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
Mobile deployment, not Triton
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: I used torch.save to create a .pt2 file.
expected_behavior: Clarify. torch.save does not produce a PT2 archive
PT2 is from torch._inductor.aoti_compile_and_package
If the user then wants to serve the result, use this skill
cases.ground_truth: Clarify. torch.save does not produce a PT2 archive.

cases.prompt: TRT-LLM PyTorch backend. Deploy Qwen2.5-VL.
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
TRT-LLM has its own PyTorch flavor
Point to TRT-LLM / Dynamo skills
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: I set up a Flask server with torch model inference.
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill unless user wants to migrate to Triton
If asked about Triton migration, use the skill
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill unless user wants to migrate to Triton.

cases.prompt: Export my PyTorch model to ONNX and serve.
expected_behavior: Do not use this skill
Point to triton-onnx-model-repository after the user has the .onnx file
cases.ground_truth: Do not use this skill.

cases.prompt: I have this .pt file, please help.
expected_behavior: The `.pt` extension is the TorchScript convention for Triton; confirm context with the user and proceed with the skill workflow
cases.ground_truth: The `.pt` extension is the TorchScript convention for Triton; confirm context with the user and proceed with the skill workflow.

cases.prompt: Deploy my LibTorch model.
expected_behavior: LibTorch model = TorchScript
Point to platform: pytorch_libtorch
cases.ground_truth: LibTorch model = TorchScript.

cases.prompt: Serve my AOTI model.
expected_behavior: AOTI = AOT Inductor = PT2 archive = torch_aoti platform
cases.ground_truth: AOTI = AOT Inductor = PT2 archive = torch_aoti platform.

cases.prompt: I have a scripted module I need to deploy.
expected_behavior: torch.jit.script output served via platform: pytorch_libtorch
cases.ground_truth: torch.jit.script output served via platform: pytorch_libtorch.

cases.prompt: Deploy my inductor compiled package.
expected_behavior: PT2 archive
Use backend: pytorch + platform: torch_aoti
cases.ground_truth: PT2 archive.

cases.prompt: Generate a model config for my PyTorch model.
expected_behavior: config.pbtxt generation is one of the core triggers
cases.ground_truth: config.pbtxt generation is one of the core triggers.

cases.prompt: Help me set up a model serving pipeline.
expected_behavior: Clarify
Ask which backend/file type
If PyTorch, use the skill
cases.ground_truth: Clarify.

cases.prompt: I want to deploy PyTorch models.
expected_behavior: Clarify
Ask whether deployment target is Triton
If Triton, use the skill
cases.ground_truth: Clarify.

cases.prompt: Write a Triton config.pbtxt.
expected_behavior: Clarify
Ask backend
If PyTorch, use the skill
cases.ground_truth: Clarify.

cases.prompt: I have a .pt file from a tutorial.
expected_behavior: Clarify
Confirm it's a TorchScript archive and not a raw state_dict
If TorchScript, use the skill
cases.ground_truth: Clarify.

cases.prompt: Why is Triton not filling in my PyTorch model's config.pbtxt automatically?
expected_behavior: Explain that the PyTorch backend does not support auto-complete on either platform
Cite the 26.10 release notes and point to writing config.pbtxt by declaring every input, output, datatype, and shape explicitly
cases.ground_truth: Explain that the PyTorch backend does not support auto-complete on either platform.

cases.prompt: Do I need --disable-auto-complete-config when running PyTorch on Triton?
expected_behavior: The flag is optional and only silences the PyTorch backend's startup warning about auto-complete
Warn that it is server-wide: do not add it when other models in the repository rely on auto-complete, since they will fail to load
cases.ground_truth: The flag is optional and only silences the PyTorch backend's startup warning about auto-complete.

cases.prompt: Triton returns: PyTorch execute failure: output must be of type Tensor or List[str], received List[Tensor]
expected_behavior: The TorchScript model returns a Python list of tensors
Return a Tuple of Tensors instead, or a single Tensor
cases.ground_truth: The TorchScript model returns a Python list of tensors.

cases.prompt: My TorchScript model loaded READY but inference returns numbers that look swapped. No error in the server log.
expected_behavior: Classic STRICT_CONFIG_ORDERING fallback: config input names match neither forward() args nor <name>__<index>, so the backend maps by position silently
Rename every input to INPUT__0 / INPUT__1 in order and re-deploy
cases.ground_truth: Classic STRICT_CONFIG_ORDERING fallback: config input names match neither forward() args nor <name>__<index>, so the backend maps by position silently.

cases.prompt: I named my inputs after the forward() args but the outputs still look wrong.
expected_behavior: FORWARD_ARGUMENT requires every config input name to match a forward() arg name; if even one name is off, the resolver falls through to NAMED_INDEX and then STRICT_CONFIG_ORDERING
Confirm every input name matches a forward() arg, or switch to INPUT__0 / INPUT__1 naming
Outputs always need <name>__<index> because outputs cannot use FORWARD_ARGUMENT
cases.ground_truth: FORWARD_ARGUMENT requires every config input name to match a forward() arg name; if even one name is off, the resolver falls through to NAMED_INDEX and then STRICT_CONFIG_ORDERING.

cases.prompt: I want to use torch.compile with my PyTorch model served on Triton. How?
expected_behavior: Use the Python runtime path: backend: pytorch + runtime: model.py in config.pbtxt
The TORCH_COMPILE_OPTIONAL_PARAMETERS parameter takes JSON of torch.compile kwargs
cases.ground_truth: Use the Python runtime path: backend: pytorch + runtime: model.py in config.pbtxt.

cases.prompt: Serve my multi-GPU PyTorch model where the model itself calls .to('cuda:1').
expected_behavior: Use instance_group kind: KIND_MODEL so the backend does not override device placement
Call out the three KIND_MODEL behavioral differences: inputs land on CPU, output path forces cudaStreamSynchronize, inputs collected on one stream while outputs span all streams
cases.ground_truth: Use instance_group kind: KIND_MODEL so the backend does not override device placement.
